questions.text: Which layers of the OSI reference model are host-to-host layers?
questions.solution:
The lower layers (physical, data link, network) work hop by hop. The upper layers from transport to application work end to end between hosts.

Answer: Transport, session, presentation, application

questions.text:
A router uses the following routing table:
[latex]\begin{array}{|l|l|l|} \hline \text { Destination } & \text { Mask } & \text { Interface } \\ \hline 144.16 .0 .0 & 255.255 .0 .0 & \text { eth0 } \\ \hline 144.16 .64 .0 & 255.255 .224 .0 & \text { eth1 } \\ \hline 144.16 .68 .0 & 255.255 .255 .0 & \text { eth2 } \\ \hline 144.16 .68 .64 & 255.255 .255 .224 & \text { eth3 } \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
Packet bearing a destination address 144.16.68.117 arrives at the router. On which interface will it be forwarded?
questions.solution:
144.16.68.117:
- eth3 (/27, 144.16.68.64): covers .64-.95 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 117 not in it
- eth2 (/24, 144.16.68.0): matches
- eth1 (/19) and eth0 (/16) also match but are shorter

Longest prefix match [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] eth2

Answer: eth2

If the machine is connected and running a TCP/IP protocol stack, it should respond to the PING datagram with a datagram of its own
If PING encounters an error condition, an ICMP message is not returned

questions.text: A certain population of ALOHA users manages to generate 70 request/sec. If the time is slotted in units of 50 msec, then channel load would be
questions.solution:
Load G = requests per slot = 70 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.05 = 3.5

Answer: 3.5

questions.text:
In a class B subnet, we know the IP address of one host and the mask as given below:
IP address: 125.134.112.66
Mask: 255.255.224.0
What is the first address(Network address)?
questions.solution:
AND the address with the mask:
- Third octet: 112 AND 224 = 96 (01110000 AND 11100000 = 01100000)
- Fourth octet: 66 AND 0 = 0

Network address = 125.134.96.0

Answer: 125.134.96.0
